text: I built a small daily game where Claude mixes 3 GitHub repos into product ideas, and each week the community picks one we build as open source. Repo Safari is a tiny daily game for finding open source projects. You walk a trail of categories and collect repos as stickers. The new part is the Idea Shower. Pick any 3 repos and press Mix, and Claude turns them into three product ideas: one useful, one unexpected and one ridiculous. If you like one, publish it to the Idea Board, where people can star the ideas they want built. Every Monday at 00:00 UTC, the idea with the most new stars that week gets built as an open source prototype. Free; playing and generating ideas need no account. Publishing and starring use GitHub sign in.
label: showcase

text: I asked Claude for a kawaii effect when I click. My video editor had no such effect. Now it does. I maintain OpenScreen, a free and open source screen recorder and video editor. Since 2.1 there's no catalog for visual effects. You describe what you want, Claude Code writes it as a small GPU shader through OpenScreen's MCP server, and it lands on the timeline as a clip. Same pixels in the preview and in the export. In the video I typed three short requests on three themed sites: kawaii effect when I click, laser effect when I click, 8 bit explosion when I click. None of these existed before. Claude wrote the code on the spot.
label: showcase

text: I had Claude build a very simple mental math game similar to Wordle. The goal is to guess hidden numbers doing mental math. You are given a starting number. You have to keep adding numbers in rows to figure out the hidden number. Each row adds to the result from all of the previous rows additions. If in any column the digit in the addition result is one of the digits of the hidden number then the background turns yellow. If that digit is in the same column as in the hidden number the background turns green and the column is solved. You win if you solve all columns before you run out of rows.
label: showcase
